# ggsurvfit

## Introduction

The **ggsurvfit** package eases the creation of time-to-event (aka
survival) summary figures with ggplot2. The concise and modular code
creates images that are ready for publication or sharing. Competing
risks cumulative incidence is also supported via
[`ggcuminc()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/ggcuminc.md).

## Why ggsurvfit?

- **Use ggplot2 functions:** Each **ggsurvfit** add-on function
  (e.g. [`add_confidence_interval()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/add_confidence_interval.md),
  [`add_risktable()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/add_risktable.md),
  etc.) is written as a proper ggplot2
  [‘geom’](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/index.html), meaning
  the package functions can be woven with ggplot2 functions seamlessly.
  You don’t need to learn how to style the plot within the ggsurvfit
  functions: rather, rely on the suite of ggplot2 functions you already
  know.

- **Publishable Legends:** Raw variable names do not appear in the
  figure legend, e.g. `"sex=Female"`.

- **Limitless Customization:** You can modify the x-axis scales or any
  other plot feature and the risk table will still align with the plot.

- **Simple Saving:** Save individual images easily with
  [`ggplot2::ggsave()`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/reference/ggsave.html).

## Installation

Install **ggsurvfit** from CRAN with:

``` r
install.packages("ggsurvfit")
```

You can install the development version from
[GitHub](https://github.com/pharmaverse/ggsurvfit) with:

``` r
# install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("pharmaverse/ggsurvfit")
```

## Examples

Review the [**figure
gallery**](https://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/articles/gallery.html)
for many more examples.

The code below constructs a basic {ggsurvfit} figure without
customization.

``` r
library(ggsurvfit)
#> Loading required package: ggplot2

p <- survfit2(Surv(time, status) ~ surg, data = df_colon) |>
  ggsurvfit(linewidth = 1) +
  add_confidence_interval() +
  add_risktable() +
  add_quantile(y_value = 0.6, color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.75) +
  scale_ggsurvfit()
```

Any figure created with {ggsurvfit} can be customized using {ggplot2}
functions.

``` r
p +
  # limit plot to show 8 years and less
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 8)) +
  # update figure labels/titles
  labs(
    y = "Percentage Survival",
    title = "Recurrence by Time From Surgery to Randomization",
  )
```

![](reference/figures/README-unnamed-chunk-2-1.png)

## `survfit2()` vs `survfit()`

Both functions have identical inputs, so why do we need
[`survfit2()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/survfit2.md)?
The
[`survfit2()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/survfit2.md)
tracks the environment from which the function was called, resulting in
the following benefits.

- We can reliably remove the raw variable names from the figure legend,
  e.g. `SEX=Female`.
- P-values can be calculated with `survfit_p()` and added to figures.
- The items above are often *possible* using
  [`survfit()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/survival/man/survfit.html). However,
  by utilizing the calling
  [environment](https://adv-r.hadley.nz/environments.html) we are
  assured the correct elements are found, rather than crossing our
  fingers that the search path contains the needed elements.

## CDISC ADaM ADTTE

The package also includes gems for those using the [CDISC ADaM ADTTE
v1.0](https://www.cdisc.org/standards/foundational/adam/adam-basic-data-structure-bds-time-event-tte-analyses-v1-0)
data model.

If columns `"PARAM"` or `"PARAMCD"` are present in the data frame passed
to
[`survfit2()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/survfit2.md),
their values will be used to construct default labels in the
[`ggsurvfit()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/ggsurvfit.md)
figure.

The event indicator in ADTTE data sets is named `"CNSR"` and is coded in
the opposite way the survival package expects outcomes—`1 = 'censored'`
and `0 = 'event'`. This difference creates an opportunity for errors to
be introduced in an analysis. The **ggsurvfit** package exports a
function called
[`Surv_CNSR()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/Surv_CNSR.md)
to resolve this concern. The function creates a survival object
(e.g. [`survival::Surv()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/survival/man/Surv.html))
that uses CDISC ADaM ADTTE coding conventions as the default values. The
function can be used in **ggsurvfit** as well as any other package that
uses [`survival::Surv()`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/survival/man/Surv.html).

``` r
survfit(Surv_CNSR() ~ 1, adtte)
#> Call: survfit(formula = Surv_CNSR() ~ 1, data = adtte)
#> 
#>         n events median 0.95LCL 0.95UCL
#> [1,] 2199    755    3.2     3.1    3.56
```

# Package index

## Build survfit

- [`survfit2()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/survfit2.md)
  : Create survival curves

## Build Plot

- [`ggsurvfit()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/ggsurvfit.md)
  : Plot Survival Probability
- [`ggcuminc()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/ggcuminc.md)
  : Plot Cumulative Incidence

## Add to Plot

- [`add_confidence_interval()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/add_confidence_interval.md)
  : Add Confidence Interval
- [`add_risktable()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/add_risktable.md)
  : Add risk table
- [`add_risktable_strata_symbol()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/add_risktable_strata_symbol.md)
  : Use Symbol for Strata in Risk Table
- [`add_quantile()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/add_quantile.md)
  : Add Quantile Annotation
- [`add_pvalue()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/add_pvalue.md)
  : Add p-value
- [`add_censor_mark()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/add_censor_mark.md)
  : Add Censor Marking
- [`add_legend_title()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/add_legend_title.md)
  : Add Legend Title

## Themes

- [`theme_risktable_default()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/theme_risktable.md)
  [`theme_risktable_boxed()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/theme_risktable.md)
  : Risk Table Themes
- [`theme_ggsurvfit_default()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/theme_ggsurvfit.md)
  [`theme_ggsurvfit_KMunicate()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/theme_ggsurvfit.md)
  : Survfit Plot Themes

## P-values

- [`survfit2_p()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/survfit2_p.md)
  : Calculate p-value
- [`format_p()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/format_p.md)
  : Format p-value

## CDISC

- [`Surv_CNSR()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/Surv_CNSR.md)
  : Create a Survival Outcome from CDISC Data

## Utilities

- [`tidy_survfit()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/tidy_survfit.md)
  : Tidy a survfit object
- [`tidy_cuminc()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/tidy_cuminc.md)
  : Tidy a cuminc object
- [`ggsurvfit_build()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/ggsurvfit_build.md)
  : Build 'ggsurvfit' Object
- [`stat_stepribbon()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/stepribbon.md)
  [`StatStepribbon`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/stepribbon.md)
  : Step ribbon statistic
- [`scale_ggsurvfit()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/scale_ggsurvfit.md)
  : Apply Scales
- [`ggsurvfit_options`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/ggsurvfit_options.md)
  : Global Options
- [`ggsurvfit_align_plots()`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/ggsurvfit_align_plots.md)
  : Align Plots

## Data

- [`df_lung`](http://www.danieldsjoberg.com/ggsurvfit/reference/df_lung.md)
  :

  Formatted Copy of
  [`survival::lung`](https://rdrr.io/pkg/survival/man/lung.html)

  Formatted Copy of
